classifications.rationale: FocusTrace evaluates the first parseable HTML meta refresh and deterministically fails a delay greater than zero and no more than 72,000 seconds using the ACT/WCAG 2.2.1 timing boundary. Its deliberately bounded parser does not claim every browser recovery branch, so the relationship remains partial.

FocusTrace evaluates the ACT-observable user-scalable and maximum-scale viewport syntax for 200% zoom. The relationship remains partial because modern user agents can override authored restrictions and the complete Resize Text criterion can also be satisfied through contextual mechanisms outside this syntax check.
FocusTrace detects prohibited/conflicting nested native interactive structures, but axe also models accessibility-tree focus combinations beyond the current native-content subset.

FocusTrace reviews unmuted native audio/video that declares autoplay beyond the three-second threshold when no native stop/mute mechanism is observable, while preserving unknown video audio-track presence and custom controls as context. Browser autoplay policy and audio-track introspection remain bounded, so the relationship is partial.

FocusTrace checks exposed object[data] elements with the shared accessible-name computation and accepts ARIA/title naming or explicit presentation. It does not reproduce every object loading/applicability branch from the benchmark, so the relationship remains partial.

FocusTrace applies the existing image-name rule to supported image and graphics roles through the shared accessible-name computation without emitting a second image finding. Its role and AccName coverage remains deliberately bounded.

FocusTrace measures rendered overflow and checks the scrollable region or a bounded descendant set for a sequential focus entry point, while retaining REVIEW for decorative regions, external controls and browser-specific scrolling behavior. This covers the benchmark's core keyboard-access concern without overclaiming exact applicability.
FocusTrace's form-field accessible-name rule includes select elements and additional supported control families.
FocusTrace has no dedicated rule rejecting server-side image maps.

FocusTrace now checks exposed native summary controls for a non-empty accessible name using author naming and name-from-content evidence, while retaining a deliberately bounded local AccName implementation.

FocusTrace reuses the image-name rule for SVG image/graphics semantics and recognizes direct SVG title text in addition to shared ARIA/title naming evidence, while retaining bounded local role and AccName coverage.

FocusTrace validates headers IDREFs on exposed native table cells, including empty, unresolved, non-header, hidden-header and cross-table targets. Outcome and some applicability boundaries intentionally differ from the benchmark, so this is classified as overlap rather than equivalent.

FocusTrace reviews exposed table headers that cannot be associated with an observed data cell, while keeping complex or ambiguous table models contextual instead of reproducing the benchmark's exact failure contract.
FocusTrace validates explicit rendered human-language descendant lang declarations using known primary subtags, intentionally excluding flat-tree and accessible-name-only cases.
FocusTrace detects prerecorded video with missing observable caption candidates but retains REVIEW because burned-in/custom-player captions cannot be proven absent from DOM evidence.
